name: Texas
note: Unverified throughout: the official statute site could not be read from this session. As cited, the funeral director files the death certificate with the local registrar within 10 days through the Texas Electronic Vital Events Registrar (TxEVER), after the attending physician or, for reportable deaths, the justice of the peace or medical examiner certifies the cause. Election Code § 16.001 sends death abstracts to voter registrars and the Secretary of State. Certified copies are restricted, and death records become public 25 years after death.

citations.title: Death Investigation by Justice of the Peace

steps.title: Death is determined by a physician (or a registered nurse where permitted)
steps.who: A physician, or a registered nurse in the circumstances the Health and Safety Code allows.
steps.summary: Texas defines when a person is dead in Health and Safety Code ch. 671, which also covers determinations by registered nurses. The text could not be read to confirm the conditions.

steps.title: Justice of the peace or medical examiner holds an inquest into a reportable death
steps.who: Law enforcement and others who learn of the death report it to the justice of the peace (inquest officer) or, in counties with one, the medical examiner.
steps.trigger: Deaths that are unattended, violent, sudden, suspicious, or otherwise listed in Code of Criminal Procedure ch. 49.
steps.summary: Texas uses justices of the peace as inquest officers except in counties with a medical examiner. The inquest officer certifies the cause in these cases.

steps.title: Attending physician, justice of the peace or medical examiner completes the medical certification
steps.who: The physician who last attended the decedent, or the inquest officer in inquest cases.
steps.trigger: The funeral director presents the certificate through the electronic registration system.

deadline.text: within the time set by § 193.005 (not confirmed)

steps.summary: The medical certification of cause of death is supplied by the attending physician or the inquest officer.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with the local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as one who is in charge of the body; if there is none, another person the statute names.

deadline.text: not later than the 10th day after the date of death

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the local registrar of the district where the death occurred, through the state's electronic vital events registrar (TxEVER).

steps.title: Burial-transit permit before disposition or removal
steps.summary: A burial-transit permit is required before the body is disposed of or moved out of the registration district.

steps.title: Local registrar sends an abstract of adult death certificates to the voter registrar
steps.who: The local registrar of births and deaths, to the county voter registrar.
steps.trigger: Death certificates of persons 18 or older filed in the county.
steps.summary: The voter registrar cancels the registration of a voter shown to have died.

steps.title: State vital statistics unit sends death abstracts to the Secretary of State
steps.who: The Department of State Health Services vital statistics unit, to the Secretary of State, who passes matches to county voter registrars.
steps.trigger: Death certificates of adults registered with the state.
steps.summary: A statewide abstract lets the Secretary of State match deaths against the statewide voter file and notify county voter registrars.

steps.title: Certified copies restricted for 25 years after death
steps.who: The state registrar or a local registrar.
steps.trigger: Application by a qualified applicant and fee.
steps.summary: Certified copies are issued under § 191.051 to applicants with a qualifying interest. Death records are confidential under the Public Information Act until 25 years after death, when they become public.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Not later than the 10th day after death (HSC § 193.003); not confirmed from the text.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or person acting as such files (HSC § 193.002); not confirmed from the text.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; inquest by justice of the peace or medical examiner only for reportable deaths.

electronicRegistration.note: Texas Electronic Vital Events Registrar (TxEVER); statutory basis in HSC ch. 193 not confirmed from the text.

governmentPropagation.note: Election Code § 16.001 death abstracts to voter registrars and the Secretary of State; SSA feeds are in the federal layer. Not confirmed from the text.

certificateAccess.note: Qualified applicants only; death records public 25 years after death (Gov't Code § 552.115). Not confirmed from the text.

gaps: Every Texas citation is unverified. statutes.capitol.texas.gov now serves a client-rendered Angular shell (250,874 bytes, no statute text) for every path; WebFetch got the same navigation-only page. Its JavaScript loads text from an API on tcss.legis.texas.gov, but fetching from that host was refused by this session's permission classifier, so it was not tried.

Other official hosts for the same text are refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403): capitol.texas.gov, tlc.texas.gov, www.sos.state.tx.us, texreg.sos.state.tx.us (Texas Administrative Code, 25 TAC ch. 181), www.dshs.texas.gov, and the mirror www.law.cornell.edu.

Section numbers in ch. 193 (193.002 duty to file, 193.003 10-day filing, 193.005 medical certification, 193.008 burial-transit permit), Election Code § 16.001 and Gov't Code § 552.115 come from the task pointers and general knowledge, not from reading the text; the medical-certification deadline and the § 16.001 frequencies especially need checking.

Not researched for lack of a readable source: Department of Public Safety driver licence cancellation on death, Health and Human Services Commission (Medicaid) death matching, any statutory state feed to SSA, nurse pronouncement conditions under HSC ch. 671, and offences for late filing.
